# infisical_alert (Resource)

Create and manage alerts that notify you about a resource in Infisical. An alert watches one event, either on a single resource or across a whole scope, depending on its resource type. A resource can only have one alert per event within a scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    infisical = {
      # version = <latest version>
      source = "infisical/infisical"
    }
  }
}

provider "infisical" {
  host = "https://app.infisical.com" # Only required if using self hosted instance of Infisical, default is https://app.infisical.com
  auth = {
    universal = {
      client_id     = "<machine-identity-client-id>"
      client_secret = "<machine-identity-client-secret>"
    }
  }
}

# Email the security team 30 days before an organization level machine identity's
# authentication credentials expire
resource "infisical_alert" "ci_identity" {
  resource_type = "identity.authentication"
  resource_id   = "<your-machine-identity-id>" # A machine identity, for this resource type
  name          = "CI identity credentials expiring"
  description   = "Rotate the CI machine identity client secret before it expires"

  # The condition block is what the alert fires on, and every alert carries exactly one. It is named
  # after the shape of the condition, so resource_type is what says what expires.
  expiry = {
    alert_before_days = 30
  }

  # Each channel is keyed by a name of your choosing, and the block it carries is what gives it
  # its type. The key is never sent to Infisical: it is only how Terraform recognizes the
  # channel, so its name can be changed freely. Changing the key, on the other hand, deletes the
  # channel and creates a new one, which notifies about everything that is still expiring, even
  # if the old one already did.
  channels = {
    security_team = {
      name = "Security team"
      email = {
        recipients = [
          {
            type = "user"
            id   = "<your-user-id>"
          },
          {
            type = "group"
            id   = "<your-group-id>"
          },
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

# Remind a project level machine identity's owners every day for the last week, over
# Slack, a signed webhook and PagerDuty
resource "infisical_alert" "deploy_identity" {
  resource_type = "identity.authentication"
  resource_id   = "<your-machine-identity-id>"
  project_id    = "<your-project-id>" # Required for resources that belong to a project
  name          = "Deploy identity credentials expiring"

  expiry = {
    alert_before_days = 7
    daily_reminder    = true
  }

  channels = {
    platform_slack = {
      name = "Platform Slack"
      slack = {
        webhook_url = "https://hooks.slack.com/services/<your-slack-webhook-path>"
      }
    }

    internal_automation = {
      name = "Internal automation"
      webhook = {
        url            = "https://example.com/infisical-alerts"
        signing_secret = "<signing-secret>" # Optional: used to sign the payload so the receiver can verify it
      }
    }

    on_call = {
      name    = "On-call"
      enabled = false # Configured up front, but not paging anyone yet
      pagerduty = {
        integration_key = "<your-pagerduty-events-api-v2-integration-key>"
      }
    }
  }
}

# Certificate Manager alerts use the same resource. This one emails a team before any certificate in
# an application expires. See the Certificate alerts guide for alerts across Certificate Manager,
# filters and code signing signer alerts.
resource "infisical_alert" "payments_certificates_expiring" {
  resource_type = "cert-manager.application"
  resource_id   = "<your-certificate-manager-application-id>"
  name          = "Payments certificates expiring"

  expiry = {
    alert_before_days = 60 # Up to 365 for certificate alerts
  }

  channels = {
    payments_team = {
      name = "Payments team"
      email = {
        recipients = [
          { type = "user", id = "<your-user-id>" },
          { type = "email", id = "payments-oncall@example.com" }, # Must be on a verified domain
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channels` (Attributes Map) The channels the alert is delivered to, keyed by a name of your choosing. The key is what identifies a channel to Terraform and is never sent to Infisical, so renaming a channel updates it in place and it keeps the deliveries it has already made. Changing a key, on the other hand, deletes the channel and creates a new one, so the new channel notifies about everything that is still expiring, even if the old one already did. Each channel carries exactly one configuration block, and that block is what gives the channel its type. At least one and at most 10 channels are allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels))
- `name` (String) The name of the alert.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of the resource to watch. Options: cert-manager, cert-manager.application, cert-manager.signer, identity.authentication.

### Optional

- `description` (String) An optional description of the alert.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert is evaluated. Defaults to true.
- `expiry` (Attributes) Fires before something the alert watches expires. Only for alerts on these resource types: cert-manager, cert-manager.application, cert-manager.signer, identity.authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--expiry))
- `filters` (Attributes) Narrows the alert to some of what it watches, which has to match every list that is set. Only for alerts on these resource types: cert-manager. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `issuance` (Attributes) Fires each time something the alert watches is issued. It takes no settings, so write it as `issuance = {}`. Only for alerts on these resource types: cert-manager, cert-manager.application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--issuance))
- `project_id` (String) The ID of the project the resource belongs to. Required for project level resources, and must be omitted for organization level ones. Not used by these resource types, so leave it out: cert-manager, cert-manager.application, cert-manager.signer.
- `renewal` (Attributes) Fires each time something the alert watches is renewed. It takes no settings, so write it as `renewal = {}`. Only for alerts on these resource types: cert-manager, cert-manager.application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--renewal))
- `resource_id` (String) The ID of the resource to watch, of the kind resource_type names. Required, except for resource types that watch a whole scope, where it must be omitted: cert-manager, cert-manager.signer.
- `revocation` (Attributes) Fires each time something the alert watches is revoked. It takes no settings, so write it as `revocation = {}`. Only for alerts on these resource types: cert-manager, cert-manager.application. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--revocation))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the alert.
- `org_id` (String) The ID of the organization the alert belongs to. Always set, whether the alert is scoped to the organization or to a project, so it is what tells you which organization a project level alert was created under.

<a id="nestedatt--channels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels`

Required:

- `name` (String) The name the channel is shown under in Infisical.

Optional:

- `email` (Attributes) Notifies principals of your organization or project by email. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels--email))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the channel delivers notifications. Defaults to true.
- `pagerduty` (Attributes) Creates PagerDuty incidents through the Events API v2. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels--pagerduty))
- `slack` (Attributes) Posts notifications to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels--slack))
- `webhook` (Attributes) Sends notifications to an HTTPS endpoint as a CloudEvents payload. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels--webhook))

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) The ID of the channel in Infisical.

<a id="nestedatt--channels--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels.email`

Required:

- `recipients` (Attributes Set) The principals to notify. At least one and at most 20 are allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels--email--recipients))

<a id="nestedatt--channels--email--recipients"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels.email.recipients`

Required:

- `id` (String) The ID of the recipient user or group, which must belong to the scope the alert is created in. For an email recipient this is the email address, which must be on one of your organization's verified email domains.
- `type` (String) The type of the recipient. Options: user, group, email. The email type is only for cert-manager, cert-manager.application, cert-manager.signer alerts.



<a id="nestedatt--channels--pagerduty"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels.pagerduty`

Required:

- `integration_key` (String, Sensitive) The PagerDuty Events API v2 integration key incidents are created with, a 32 character hex string. Write-only: it is never returned by the API, so it cannot be imported.


<a id="nestedatt--channels--slack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels.slack`

Required:

- `webhook_url` (String, Sensitive) The Slack incoming webhook URL notifications are posted to. Must be a https://hooks.slack.com URL. Write-only: it is never returned by the API, so it cannot be imported.


<a id="nestedatt--channels--webhook"></a>
### Nested Schema for `channels.webhook`

Required:

- `url` (String) The HTTPS URL the CloudEvents payload is sent to.

Optional:

- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) The secret used to sign the payload so the receiver can verify it. Write-only: it is never returned by the API, so an imported channel keeps the secret it was created with until one is set here.



<a id="nestedatt--expiry"></a>
### Nested Schema for `expiry`

Required:

- `alert_before_days` (Number) How many days before expiry the alert fires. Must be at least 1, and at most 90 for identity.authentication; 365 for cert-manager, cert-manager.application, cert-manager.signer.

Optional:

- `daily_reminder` (Boolean) Whether to keep notifying once a day until expiry, instead of notifying once. Defaults to false.


<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Optional:

- `application_ids` (Set of String) Only certificates in these Certificate Manager applications. Leave it out to cover all of them. At most 100.
- `profile_ids` (Set of String) Only certificates issued from these certificate profiles. Leave it out to cover all of them. At most 100.
- `sources` (Set of String) Only certificates with these sources. Options: issued, discovered, imported. Leave it out to cover every source.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import infisical_alert.example <alert_id>

# An imported alert keys each of its channels by the name it has in Infisical, so write the
# channels in your configuration under those same keys, or the import deletes them and creates
# new ones that notify about everything still expiring, even though the imported channels
# already did. The keys are yours to choose from then on, since only the name attribute reaches
# Infisical.
#
# Write-only channel secrets (a Slack webhook URL, a PagerDuty integration key, a webhook
# signing secret) are never returned by the API, so the first plan after an import shows them
# being set. A signing secret left out of the configuration keeps whatever is stored.
```
